name: mission-control-mods
title: Mission Control mods
overview: One standalone mod, mission-control-mods, manages the mods and layouts installed in the Herdr app home: it lists them, shows which have a newer version on GitHub, updates them with a review first, and disables, enables and uninstalls them. Like GitHub and Jira it installs on its own or as the seventh work source (Mods) in both Mission Control layouts. Its origins come from the herdr.dev catalog (assets.herdr.dev mods and layouts indexes, built from the public herdr-mod and herdr-layout GitHub topics) and from per-file git blob hashes, because no Herdr listing carries a version.
scopeChallenge: Scope follows the user's request (list, detect new versions, update, enable/disable, uninstall for mods and layouts) and the published practice of four existing community managers (manastalukdar/herdr-pkg, jacksonpires/herdr-app-mod-manager, atleugim/herdr-mod-manager, linziyanleo Mods Plus), adopting their working mechanisms and avoiding their documented failures. Installing new items from the gallery is out of scope for this plan; the catalog is used only to identify and update what is already installed.
prerequisites: Herdr app 0.1.11+ with hc 0.1.16+; re-read the installed ~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md, herdr.d.ts and gpui-kit.d.ts before execution and stop on incompatible contracts.
The founder (the user) approves this plan at its current JSON and Markdown hashes before implementation.

Node.js 22+ on this computer for the helper (same requirement as the Jira, GitHub and GitLab helpers) and git for partial clones and three-way merges. No GitHub account or token is used: only public repositories are read.
nonGoals: No installing new items from the gallery; no publishing; no rating or reporting.
No management of Herdr's shipped mods and layouts (the keys of appHome()/installed.json): they are listed read-only as Built into Herdr, because Herdr restores and updates them itself.
No editing of shipped layouts, no automatic layout switching, no change to Herdr settings.
No credentials: only public github.com repositories are read through git with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; private repositories are reported as unreachable.
Not a security reviewer: the capability scan is a disclosure of what the files reach, never a proof of safety.
contracts: Native GPUI JavaScript only in main.js; every network, git, file and herdr-app check operation runs in the Node helper (node <appHome>/mods/mission-control-mods/backend.mjs, the same launch as the GitHub helper) through exec, which Herdr limits to 30 s and 8 MiB: each helper call is bounded to 25 s and long work is split into resumable passes.

Records live in appHome()/mission-control/mods/ (packages.json, journal.json, log.jsonl, cache/, stage/, backup/, disabled/, removed/, conflicts/), following this repository's appHome()/mission-control/ convention, not Herdr's own data/ folder. Backups keep the newest three per item.

Writes to packages.json, journal.json and keys.json are temp-file-plus-rename under a lock whose stale timeout is 60 s (longer than the 25 s helper bound plus a margin) (a Node helper cannot use Herdr's writeTextFile compare-and-set). Changes to mods/, layouts/ or keys.json are journalled first and rolled forward or back at the next helper start.

Classification: built-in = keys of installed.json; personal clone = mod.json cloned_from; installer-managed = files listed in appHome()/mission-control/installed-packages.json, the ownership manifest scripts/install.mjs writes on install and removes on rollback (updated with the installer, shown read-only); without that manifest Mission Control items count as installed by hand and are managed like any user item; this manager = mission-control-mods itself (read-only). Only user items are updated, disabled or removed.

Origin: the catalog at https://assets.herdr.dev/{mods,layouts}/index.json (built hourly by herdr.dev from the public herdr-mod and herdr-layout GitHub topics) matched on modNames/layoutFiles, never repo names; an item's subtree is <path>/mods/<name>/, <path>/layouts/<file> and <path>/keys.json; the commit whose tree holds every installed blob wins; several candidates without one are ambiguous; none is untracked until a pasted GitHub link. Several exact matches (identical forks) prefer the repository already recorded for the item, otherwise the item is ambiguous until the user picks once. Items adopted from a pasted link are re-checked with git ls-remote.

Git, not the GitHub API: blob-less partial clones (git clone --filter=blob:none) read history, trees and blobs without rate limits; only items whose catalog headCommit changed are re-checked; github.com URLs only, except file:// and a QA catalog URL under QA_MODS_FIXTURE=1 for the native gate. A clone or fetch that cannot finish within one call continues as a detached git process with a status file; after three failed passes the item reads too large or slow to fetch.
Update available means a commit touching the item's subtree changed, added or removed a file relative to the recorded commit; a repository commit elsewhere is not an update.

Updates stage outside mods/, merge edited text files with git merge-file, treat edited binary files as conflicts, show a review, pass herdr-app check on the stage, then write changed files in place (hot reload watches the installed folder) and delete only unedited removed files. A conflict writes nothing and offers Keep mine, Take theirs or Open the merged files.
keys.json: an item's bindings are added only where free or already equal; every added key is recorded; update and uninstall change or remove a key only while it still equals what the item set.

Disable and uninstall are journalled moves to disabled/ and removed/<name>/<time>/, restorable, and removed items older than 30 days are pruned at the next check; refused for built-in, installer-managed and self items, the active layout and mods the active layout uses; other referencing layouts are named and confirmed.

Mods is a work source with a fixed All installed scope and caption, reusing an existing icon so icons.json and the other packages are unchanged; with seven sources the strip uses short labels at 1024 px.

tasks.title: Read the catalog and source repositories without API quota
tasks.description: Fetch https://assets.herdr.dev/{mods,layouts}/index.json (one-hour cache) and keep a blob-less partial clone of each referenced github.com repository (git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout, then git fetch) under appHome()/mission-control/mods/cache/, reading history, trees and individual blobs through git so no GitHub API rate limit applies. Every call is bounded to finish inside one exec; a QA_MODS_CATALOG_URL and file:// remotes are honoured only when QA_MODS_FIXTURE=1, for the native gate. A fetch that cannot finish within one call continues detached with a status file and ends as too large or slow to fetch after three failed passes; git runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
acceptanceCriteria: Catalog entries with empty and nested path both resolve; a non-github.com URL is refused outside the fixture mode; truncated or failed fetches keep the previous cache with a stated reason.
A path-scoped history query, a tree read and a blob read work from the partial clone with no network call once fetched; each call returns inside 25 s or reports that it needs another pass.

writeScope.role: Catalog cache and git partial-clone reads (history, trees, blobs), bounded per exec, with fixture overrides.
Local bare repositories and a fixture catalog for paths, caching, refusal and time bounds.

tasks.title: Crash-safe records, locks and an intent journal
tasks.description: Records live in appHome()/mission-control/mods/ (packages.json, journal.json, log.jsonl). Every write is a temp file plus rename under a lock file with a stale timeout. Any change to mods/, layouts/ or keys.json is preceded by a journal entry listing each planned file operation and its backup; every helper start first rolls an open journal forward or back. Temp files use hidden names outside the watched folders.
acceptanceCriteria: Killing the helper at any point during a journalled commit leaves, after the next helper start, either the complete old or the complete new state of every touched file and of keys.json.
Two helpers racing on packages.json never lose an update; a stale lock is reclaimed only after its timeout.

writeScope.role: Lock, temp-plus-rename writes, intent journal and recovery.
Real child processes killed mid-commit, concurrent writers and stale locks.

tasks.title: Inventory installed items and adopt their origins
tasks.description: List mods/* and layouts/*.json; classify built-in (installed.json keys), personal clones (cloned_from), installer-managed (listed in appHome()/mission-control/installed-packages.json; without it, Mission Control items are treated as installed by hand), the manager itself, disabled and user items; hash every file as a git blob. Match an item by folder name against catalog modNames or layoutFiles (and a layout entry folder's mods/), define its subtree as <path>/mods/<name>/, <path>/layouts/<file> and <path>/keys.json, and choose among candidates: the commit whose tree holds every installed blob wins; with several candidates and no exact match the item is ambiguous and lists them; with none it is untracked until the user pastes a GitHub folder link.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture app home with built-in, clone, installer-managed, self, exact, older-commit, edited, ambiguous, disabled and unknown items yields exactly those states.
A layout and the mods in its folder are recorded as one package; built-in, clone, installer-managed and self items never get an origin.

writeScope.role: Scan, classification, blob hashing, catalog matching and adoption.
Fixture app homes against local bare repositories and a fixture catalog.

tasks.title: Detect new versions per item
tasks.description: Re-check only items whose catalog headCommit changed since the last check: find the newest commit touching the item's subtree and compare its tree with the recorded commit (added, changed, removed files), with that commit's date and subject. Items adopted from a pasted link are re-checked with git ls-remote.
acceptanceCriteria: A repository commit outside the subtree is not an update; an added, changed or removed file inside it is, listing the files.
An unchanged catalog headCommit costs no git fetch, an item adopted from a pasted link is re-checked through git ls-remote, and offline keeps the last result with its time.

writeScope.role: Subtree-scoped update detection with cached results.
Local repositories with in-path and out-of-path commits, removals and offline.

tasks.title: Update with a review, a three-way merge and a journalled commit
tasks.description: Phase 1 (one exec, outside mods/): stage the new version under the records folder, merge each locally edited text file with git merge-file against the recorded base, treat edited binary files as conflicts, compute the review (changed files, newly disclosed network/program/file access, key changes) and run herdr-app check on the stage. Phase 2 (one exec, local only): journal, back up, write changed files in place, delete unedited removed files, merge keys by ownership, record the new commit. A conflict writes nothing and offers Keep mine, Take theirs or Open the merged files.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean merge applies; a conflict or a binary edit writes nothing to mods/ and offers the three resolutions, each of which completes or restores.
A failing check, a write error or a killed helper leaves the installed folder and keys.json as they were (via the journal); generated *.d.ts, jsconfig.json and runtime.json are never touched.

writeScope.role: Stage, merge, review, check and journalled commit with conflict resolution.
Real git merge-file, binary conflicts, a fake herdr-app check, rollback and key ownership.

tasks.title: Disable, enable, uninstall, restore, and the helper entry point
tasks.description: Journalled moves to appHome()/mission-control/mods/disabled/ and removed/<name>/<time>/; restore from either; prune backups to the newest three per item; Restore everything before the manager is removed. Refuse built-in, installer-managed and self items, the active layout and any mod the active layout uses; ask for confirmation, naming each layout, for mods other layouts use. backend.mjs dispatches every operation in one bounded exec.
acceptanceCriteria: Disable then enable, and uninstall then restore, return identical bytes and keys; every refusal states its reason.
Each operation returns within the exec limit or reports a continuation; the entry point recovers an open journal before doing anything else.

writeScope.role: Disable, enable, uninstall, restore, pruning and reference rules.
Bounded helper entry point with journal recovery first.
Refusals, references, keys, restore and Restore everything through the entry point.

tasks.title: The Mods panel
tasks.description: Sections Updates, Layouts, Mods, Disabled and Built into Herdr; per-row status (up to date, update available with date and subject, edited, conflict, ambiguous, disabled, untracked, personal clone, managed by the installer, this manager) and actions; review screen before applying; Update all applies only clean updates without new access or key clashes; two-step Uninstall whose confirmation says removed items can be restored for 30 days and are then deleted; conflict resolution; Check now with last checked time; search; paste-a-link adoption. Caption reads All installed; runs with hideHeader in the layouts. Opening the panel first asks the helper to recover any open journal, so a half-applied change is finished or undone before anything is shown.
acceptanceCriteria: Every status renders with exactly its allowed actions, and each action calls the helper and redraws from its result.
